# Child-Safe EdTech Framework (CSEF): rule catalogue. Single source of truth.
# Generated documents (catalogue, checklists, skill references, semgrep rules)
# are built from this file by tooling/build.py. Do not edit those by hand.
#
# Field reference (see framework/00-introduction.md for the full explanation):
#   id          PREFIX-AREA-NN. Prefixes: CORE, A (educational games), B (game-based
#               applications), C (gamified applications), AGE (age-band modifiers).
#   level       MUST | SHOULD
#   tier        1 = legal baseline, 2 = forward-compliant, 3 = best practice
#   profiles    [core] applies to every product; otherwise any of [A, B, C]
#   age_bands   [all] or any of [B1, B2, B3, B4, B5]
#   features    optional. Rule only applies if the product declares one of these
#               features in its manifest (or if there is no manifest).
#   sources     ids from framework/sources.yaml or a loaded pack
#   effort      low | medium | high (used to prioritise the improvement list)
#   detection   method: static | manifest | manual | mixed, plus patterns

version: "0.8.0"

rules:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: governance
  - id: CORE-GOV-01
    title: Product declares its CSEF manifest
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The repository contains a CSEF manifest (csef.yaml) declaring profiles, age bands,
      context of use, GDPR role, features, AI use, third parties and chosen compliance level.
    rationale: >
      Accountability (GDPR Art. 5(2)) requires being able to show what the product does with
      children's data. The manifest is also what lets the checks select the right rules.
    improvement: Copy templates/csef.yaml to the repository root and fill it in with the product owner.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: manifest_missing, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-GOV-02
    title: Legal scope of the EU KIDS Act is assessed and recorded
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The manifest records whether the product is in scope of the EU KIDS Act (online game,
      AI companion, general conversational chatbot, social or video-sharing service) or exempt
      as a service designed primarily for education and operated by or on behalf of an
      educational establishment (Art. 2(4)(c)).
    rationale: >
      The same product can be exempt when deployed by a school and in scope when offered
      directly to families. Teams must know which situation they are in for each channel.
    improvement: Fill the `legal_scope.kids_act` field in csef.yaml for each distribution channel.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, KIDS-FAQ]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: kids_act_scope_missing, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-GOV-03
    title: Child rights impact assessment
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      A child rights impact assessment (or a risk review in the sense of the DSA Art. 28
      guidelines) is documented, considers the best interests of the child, and involves
      children, guardians and educators in testing.
    rationale: >
      The DSA guidelines and UN General Comment No. 25 ask providers to weigh all children's
      rights (protection, participation, provision), not only data protection.
    improvement: Extend the DPIA with a child rights section (templates/dpia-starter.md, part C).
    effort: medium
    sources: [DSA-G28, UNCRC-GC25, EUKO]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: data protection
  - id: CORE-DAT-01
    title: DPIA before launch
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      A Data Protection Impact Assessment exists before launch when children's data is processed
      at scale, with new technology (including AI), or for systematic monitoring of learners.
    rationale: Processing of vulnerable data subjects with new technology is high risk under GDPR Art. 35.
    improvement: >
      Start a DPIA with templates/dpia-starter.md. If the school or Ministry is controller, provide
      them the technical input; they sign it.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: dpia_missing, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-02
    title: Controller and processor roles are defined, with processor agreements
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The manifest states whether the provider acts as controller or processor, and every third
      party that touches personal data has a data processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28).
    rationale: Without defined roles nobody is accountable for legal basis, DPIA or data subject requests.
    improvement: "Record `gdpr_role` and `dpa_signed: true` for each third party, or remove the integration."
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: third_party_without_dpa, confidence: high}
        - {type: manifest, check: gdpr_role_missing, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-03
    title: No transfers outside the EEA without a valid mechanism
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Personal data of minors is hosted in the EEA, or every transfer outside it has a documented
      transfer mechanism (adequacy decision, SCCs plus transfer impact assessment).
    rationale: GDPR Chapter V.
    improvement: Move hosting to an EEA region or record `transfer_mechanism` for the third party.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: transfer_outside_eea, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-DAT-04
    title: No personal data in analytics events
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Analytics and telemetry events carry no direct identifiers (name, email, phone, IP address,
      precise location, free text typed by the child). Use pseudonymous IDs.
    rationale: Data minimisation and purpose limitation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)(c)).
    improvement: Replace identifiers with a pseudonymous learner ID and drop free-text fields from events.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - type: regex
          confidence: medium
          pattern: '(track|logEvent|capture|analytics\.\w+)\s*\([^)]*\b(email|e_mail|full_?name|first_?name|last_?name|phone|ip_?address|latitude|longitude)\b'
          flags: i

  - id: CORE-DAT-05
    title: Retention periods enforced by code
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Each category of learner data has a retention period, enforced by an automated deletion
      or anonymisation job, not only by policy text.
    rationale: Storage limitation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e)).
    improvement: Add a scheduled deletion job per data category and list it in csef.yaml `retention`.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: retention_missing, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-DAT-06
    title: Data subject rights are supported by tooling
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Access, rectification, erasure and export of a learner's data can be executed by tooling
      (admin function or script), and the process is tested.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 15 to 20. Schools as controllers depend on the processor to execute requests.
    improvement: Build an admin export and delete function per learner and test it each release.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-DAT-07
    title: No real learner data outside production
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Seeds, fixtures, tests, staging databases and prompts sent to development AI tools use
      synthetic data only.
    rationale: Purpose limitation and security (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)(f), Art. 32).
    improvement: Use a synthetic data generator (e.g. Faker) and block production dumps in non-production environments.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - type: regex
          confidence: medium
          globs: ['*seed*', '*fixture*', '*mock*', '*.sql', '*test*']
          pattern: '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@(gmail|hotmail|outlook|yahoo|sapo|live|icloud)\.(com|pt|es|fr|de)'
          flags: i

  - id: CORE-DAT-08
    title: No biometric identification of minors
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: The product does not process face, voice or fingerprint data to identify children.
    rationale: Biometric data for identification is special category data (GDPR Art. 9). Disproportionate in education.
    improvement: Remove face or voice recognition. Use class codes, picture passwords or teacher-managed login.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: dependency, confidence: high, names: [face-api.js, '@vladmandic/face-api', face_recognition, deepface, '@aws-sdk/client-rekognition', amazon-rekognition, azure-cognitiveservices-face, '@azure/cognitiveservices-face']}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(faceRecognition|recognizeFace|FaceMatcher|detectAllFaces|compareFaces|voiceprint|speakerRecognition)'}

  - id: CORE-DAT-09
    title: Geolocation off and not collected unless essential
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Precise geolocation is not collected. If a feature truly needs it, it is off by default
      and turned off again at the end of the session.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 11(1)(a) and 11(2) (applied to games via Art. 15(1)(b)). DSA Art. 28 guidelines on safe defaults.
    improvement: Remove location permissions or gate them behind an explicit, session-limited opt-in.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(navigator\.geolocation|getCurrentPosition|watchPosition|ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION|NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription|CLLocationManager|Input\.location\.Start)'}

  - id: CORE-DAT-10
    title: Microphone and camera off by default
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Access to microphone and camera is off by default, requested only at the moment of use
      for a clear learning purpose, and the recording is not kept longer than needed.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 11(1)(b), applied to games via Art. 15(1)(b).
    improvement: Request media permissions just-in-time with a child-friendly explanation; never at start-up.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(getUserMedia|RECORD_AUDIO|android\.permission\.CAMERA|NSMicrophoneUsageDescription|NSCameraUsageDescription|Microphone\.Start|WebCamTexture)'}

  - id: CORE-DAT-11
    title: Consent for non-essential storage and cookies
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Non-essential cookies and local storage are only set after valid consent, and where consent
      is the legal basis for minors under the national age of digital consent (13 to 16), a guardian gives it.
    rationale: ePrivacy Art. 5(3) and GDPR Art. 8.
    improvement: Keep only strictly necessary storage, or add a guardian-facing consent flow.
    effort: medium
    sources: [EPRIV, GDPR, EDPB-CONSENT]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-DAT-12
    title: Child-friendly privacy information
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Privacy information exists in a version the target age can understand (very short sentences,
      icons, audio for non-readers), plus a full version for adults.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 12(1) requires clear language, in particular for information addressed to a child.
    improvement: Write a one-screen child version of the privacy notice and test it with children of the target age.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, KIDS]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: commercial
  - id: CORE-COM-01
    title: No advertising or ad tracking SDKs
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No advertising based on profiling of minors and no ad, attribution or fingerprinting SDKs
      in products used by minors.
    rationale: DSA Art. 28(2) bans profiling-based ads to minors on online platforms. The DFA proposal extends this to all traders.
    improvement: Remove the SDK. If marketing attribution is needed, measure it on the adult-facing website only.
    effort: low
    sources: [DSA, DFA, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, globs: ['*.cs'], pattern: '\b(Advertisement\.(Initialize|Show|Load)|MobileAds\.Initialize|FB\.Init|AppsFlyer\.initSDK|IronSource\.Agent|LevelPlay\.Init|AdjustConfig)\b'}
        - type: dependency
          confidence: high
          names: [react-native-google-mobile-ads, google-mobile-ads, '@capacitor-community/admob', admob-plus-cordova, react-native-fbsdk, react-native-fbsdk-next, facebook-nodejs-business-sdk, facebook_business, react-native-appsflyer, appsflyer-capacitor-plugin, react-native-adjust, '@adjustcom/adjust-web-sdk', react-native-branch, branch-sdk, '@fingerprintjs/fingerprintjs', '@fingerprintjs/fingerprintjs-pro', Google-Mobile-Ads-SDK, FBSDKCoreKit, AppsFlyerFramework, Adjust, 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-ads', 'com.facebook.android:facebook-android-sdk', 'com.appsflyer:af-android-sdk', 'com.adjust.sdk:adjust-android', google_mobile_ads, appsflyer_sdk, adjust_sdk, com.unity.ads, com.unity.services.levelplay, com.google.ads.mobile, com.ironsource.sdk, GoogleMobileAds, Unity.Advertisements, Google.Apis.AdSense.v2]
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, pattern: '(googletagservices\.com|doubleclick\.net|connect\.facebook\.net/[^"'' ]*/fbevents\.js|adsbygoogle)'}

  - id: CORE-COM-02
    title: Third-party analytics and session recording reviewed
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Product analytics and session-replay tools are either self-hosted in the EEA or bound by a
      processor agreement that forbids reuse of data. Session recording is not used on child-facing screens.
    rationale: Many analytics vendors reuse data for their own purposes, which would make them controllers (GDPR Art. 28).
    improvement: Prefer self-hosted analytics (e.g. EU-hosted PostHog or Matomo) with IP anonymisation; remove session replay from child screens.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, globs: ['*.cs'], pattern: '\b(Firebase\.Analytics|GameAnalyticsSDK|AnalyticsService\.Instance)\b'}
        - type: dependency
          confidence: medium
          names: ['@react-native-firebase/analytics', firebase-analytics, mixpanel-browser, mixpanel-react-native, '@amplitude/analytics-browser', '@segment/analytics-next', '@hotjar/browser', '@fullstory/browser', '@microsoft/clarity', logrocket, smartlook-client, posthog-js, com.unity.services.analytics, com.unity.analytics, com.google.firebase.analytics, com.gameanalytics.sdk]
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(getAnalytics\s*\(|static\.hotjar\.com|clarity\.ms/tag)'}

  - id: CORE-COM-03
    title: No dark patterns
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No fake urgency or scarcity, confirmshaming, pre-ticked options, nagging after a choice,
      obstruction to leave or cancel, fake notifications, or confusing double negatives.
    rationale: DSA Art. 25, UCPD. The DFA proposal blacklists these in all circumstances.
    improvement: Rewrite the copy neutrally, remove timers and pre-selected options, make 'no' as easy as 'yes'.
    effort: low
    sources: [DSA, UCPD, DFA, R-RADESKY2022]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, flags: i, pattern: '(only \d+ left|offer ends in|hurry[,!]? |last chance|don''t miss out|limited time offer|só restam \d+|última oportunidade|oferta termina|despacha-te|não percas)'}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(no thanks,? i (don''t|do not) want|não,? não quero aprender|i prefer to stay (bad|behind))'}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(defaultChecked|checked)\s*=\s*\{?\s*true'}

  - id: CORE-COM-04
    title: Purchases are adult-facing only
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Children are never directly exhorted to buy, and any purchase flow is behind an adult gate
      (guardian or school account), with the price in real currency.
    rationale: UCPD Annex I point 28 (direct exhortation to children). KIDS Act Art. 13 and 14(1)(c).
    improvement: Move purchases to a guardian or school portal; remove buy prompts from child screens.
    effort: medium
    sources: [UCPD, KIDS, DFA]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, globs: ['*.cs'], pattern: '\b(UnityPurchasing\.Initialize|IDetailedStoreListener|IStoreListener|CodelessIAPStoreListener)\b'}
        - {type: dependency, confidence: medium, names: [react-native-iap, expo-in-app-purchases, '@revenuecat/purchases-js', react-native-purchases, cordova-plugin-purchase, in_app_purchase, purchases_flutter, com.unity.purchasing, com.unity.services.purchasing]}
        - {type: manifest, check: monetisation_for_minors, confidence: high}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: safety by design
  - id: CORE-SAF-01
    title: Most protective settings by default
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Profiles private, sharing off, contact off, notifications off, recommendations of other users
      off by default. Defaults are only relaxed after age assurance shows the user is an adult.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 8(1) and 11(1). DSA Art. 28 guidelines.
    improvement: Flip the defaults in the settings model and add a test that asserts them.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(isPublic|publicProfile|profileVisibility|shareEnabled|allowMessages|discoverable)\s*[:=]\s*(true|[''"]public[''"])'}

  - id: CORE-SAF-02
    title: Notifications only about the child's own activity, off by default, quiet hours
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [notifications]
    requirement: >
      Push notifications are off by default, never designed to prompt the child to start or resume
      use, only relate to the child's own activity or teacher assignments, and respect school time
      and core sleep hours.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(b) and 11(1)(d), applied to games via Art. 15(1).
    improvement: Default the push flag to false, remove re-engagement campaigns, add quiet hours (e.g. 21:00 to 08:00 and school hours).
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28, DFA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, pattern: '(push(Notifications)?Enabled|notificationsEnabled|enablePush)\s*[:=]\s*true'}
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, flags: i, pattern: '(we miss you|come back and play|your friends are waiting|it''s been a while|temos saudades|volta a jogar|os teus amigos estão à tua espera)'}

  - id: CORE-SAF-03
    title: Natural stopping points, no autoplay or endless feeds
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No autoplay of the next content and no infinite scroll. Sessions have natural endings and
      regular interruption moments that let the child decide whether to continue.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(a). DFA proposal gives users the right to switch off autoplay.
    improvement: Remove autoplay; end each activity with a clear 'done' screen and an explicit choice to continue.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DFA, DSA-G28, R-RADESKY2022]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(autoPlayNext|autoplayNext|autoplay\s*[:=]\s*true|<video[^>]*\sautoplay)'}
        - {type: dependency, confidence: medium, names: [react-infinite-scroll-component, react-infinite-scroller, ngx-infinite-scroll, vue-infinite-loading]}

  - id: CORE-SAF-04
    title: Time-awareness tools
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The product offers break reminders and lets guardians or teachers set a daily time limit,
      protecting school time (outside class use) and core sleep hours.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 9(3) and 20(4)(a) require time-limited access for social and video services. Best practice for all products.
    improvement: Add a session timer with a gentle break screen and a configurable daily limit.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, KIDS-COM]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-SAF-05
    title: No contact from strangers
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [multiplayer, chat, ugc, social]
    requirement: >
      Nobody outside the child's approved group (class, guardian-approved contacts) can initiate
      contact, see the child's profile or content, or add the child to a group.
    rationale: DSA Art. 28 and guidelines. KIDS Act Art. 12(1), applied to games via Art. 15(1)(c).
    improvement: Scope all interaction to closed groups managed by a teacher or guardian; remove user search and contact suggestions.
    effort: high
    sources: [DSA, DSA-G28, KIDS]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(searchUsers|findFriends|suggestedFriends|peopleYouMayKnow|friendSuggestions|addFriendByName|randomMatch|findRandomPlayer|joinPublicRoom|publicLobby|globalChat|worldChat)'}

  - id: CORE-SAF-06
    title: Child-friendly reporting and support
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [multiplayer, chat, ugc, social, ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      Wherever children interact with others or with generated content, a report option is one
      step away, understandable by the target age, processed with priority, and followed by
      information on help resources.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 19. DSA Art. 16 and Art. 28 guidelines.
    improvement: Add a visible report button, a priority moderation queue and a help screen with national helplines.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DSA, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-SAF-07
    title: Tools for guardians and teachers that respect the child
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Guardians (or teachers in school use) can manage settings, time and contacts. The child is
      told when such tools are active. Controls cannot be bypassed by the child.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 20, applied to online games by Art. 15(1)(d).
    improvement: Provide a guardian or teacher panel for settings, time limits and contacts, with an in-app notice to the child.
    effort: high
    sources: [KIDS, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-SAF-08
    title: Proportionate, privacy-preserving age assurance
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Where age matters, age assurance is proportionate, uses zero-knowledge solutions such as the
      EU age verification app, does not store identity documents and only keeps an age signal.
      Self-declaration alone is not relied on for high-risk features.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 27 and 28: age assurance must be accurate and privacy-preserving, and its data may
      never be used to identify, track, target, advertise to or profile the user (Art. 28(1)). Art. 31
      requires Member States to provide free EU age verification and guardian attestation means.
      DSA Art. 28 guidelines. EU age verification Recommendation.
    improvement: >
      Integrate the EU age verification solution or the EUDI wallet, and the national guardian
      attestation when available (KIDS Act Art. 31); store only an 'over threshold' flag and never
      reuse age assurance data for any other purpose.
    effort: high
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28, AVREC]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(id_?card_?(image|photo|upload)|passport_?(image|photo|upload)|upload(Id|Passport)Document)'}

  - id: CORE-SAF-09
    title: Children can control and give feedback on what they see
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [B3, B4, B5]
    requirement: >
      Children can adjust settings that affect how they interact and what they are shown, give
      feedback with lasting effect, and easily return to default settings.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 18.
    improvement: Add a simple 'my settings' screen with a 'reset to safe settings' button.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-SAF-10
    title: No social comparison or image-altering features
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No follower counts, likes on the child's appearance, beauty filters, or features that
      embellish or idealise the child's image.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 11(3).
    improvement: Remove public counters and appearance filters; use avatars instead of photos.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(followerCount|followersCount|likeCount|beautyFilter|faceFilter|skinSmooth)'}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: AI
  - id: CORE-AI-01
    title: No emotion recognition on learners
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: The product does not infer emotions of learners from face, voice, posture, typing or other biometric signals.
    rationale: AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) prohibits emotion recognition in education institutions since 2 Feb 2025.
    improvement: Remove emotion inference. Use explicit signals (a help button, a self-report mood picker).
    effort: medium
    sources: [AIA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: dependency, confidence: high, names: [fer, hume, '@humeai/voice', affdex, '@affectiva/affdex', emotion-recognition, py-feat]}
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, pattern: '(withFaceExpressions|detectEmotion|emotionRecognition|recognizeEmotion|facialExpression|sentimentFromFace|frustrationDetect)'}

  - id: CORE-AI-02
    title: No manipulative AI exploiting age
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      AI features do not use subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques, or exploit age-related
      vulnerability, to change a child's behaviour in a harmful way.
    rationale: AI Act Art. 5(1)(a)(b).
    improvement: Review prompts and reward logic for persuasion targets that serve engagement over learning; document the review.
    effort: medium
    sources: [AIA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-AI-03
    title: AI interaction and AI-generated content are disclosed
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      Children (and teachers) are told, in age-appropriate form, when they interact with AI and
      when content is AI-generated. Generated media is marked.
    rationale: AI Act Art. 50, applicable from 2 Aug 2026.
    improvement: Add a persistent 'AI' label on AI responses and metadata marking on generated images and audio.
    effort: low
    sources: [AIA]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: dependency, confidence: medium, names: [openai, '@anthropic-ai/sdk', anthropic, '@google/generative-ai', '@google/genai', google-generativeai, '@mistralai/mistralai', mistralai, groq-sdk, ai, '@ai-sdk/openai', langchain, '@langchain/core', elevenlabs, '@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js']}

  - id: CORE-AI-04
    title: AI inventory and no training on learners' data by default
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative, ai_assessment, ai_adaptive]
    requirement: >
      Every AI component is listed (model, provider, purpose, inputs, outputs, oversight). Provider
      data retention for training is disabled. Learners' data is not used to train or fine-tune
      models without a DPIA and a lawful basis.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 5 and 35. AI Act Art. 4 (AI literacy) and provider transparency.
    improvement: Create docs/ai-inventory.md and switch providers to zero-retention or no-training settings.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, AIA]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: ai_without_inventory, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-AI-05
    title: Age-appropriate AI output, tested before release
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      Input and output filters adapted to the target age, red-team tests in the product's languages
      before release, and post-release monitoring of incidents.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 14(1)(e)(f) for chatbots and companions. Best practice for any child-facing generative AI.
    improvement: Build a red-team prompt set per age band and language; run it in CI on prompt changes.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, AIA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-AI-06
    title: No AI persona that simulates a relationship
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      AI characters are friendly but never claim feelings, friendship, missing the child, or
      exclusivity, and do not create emotional dependency (see CORE-AI-08 for conversation memory).
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 3(5)(c) and 14(1)(a)(b): such a system would be an 'AI companion' in scope,
      even in an educational product. DFA proposal: right to switch off relationship-simulating chatbots.
    improvement: Rewrite the system prompt persona; add tests that reject outputs claiming feelings or friendship.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DFA, AIA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, flags: i, pattern: '(i missed you|i love you|i''m your (best )?friend|you are my (best )?friend|only i understand you|don''t leave me|tive saudades tuas|sou o teu melhor amigo|és o meu melhor amigo|não me deixes)'}

  - id: CORE-AI-07
    title: Human review of decisions about learners
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_assessment, ai_adaptive]
    requirement: >
      No grade, level placement, certification or access decision about a learner is taken solely
      by automated processing. A teacher can see, explain and override it.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 22. AI Act Annex III(3) human oversight requirements from 2 Dec 2027.
    improvement: Make automated results provisional until a teacher confirms; show the reasons.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, AIA, AIA-OMNIBUS]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: accessibility
  - id: CORE-ACC-01
    title: WCAG 2.2 AA
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Interfaces meet WCAG 2.2 level AA (aligned with EN 301 549), with automated checks in CI
      and manual screen-reader testing per release.
    rationale: European Accessibility Act for covered services; public procurement rules for schools.
    improvement: Add axe-core or Pa11y to CI and fix contrast, labels, focus order and keyboard access.
    effort: medium
    sources: [EAA, WCAG22, EN301549]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, globs: ['*.html', '*.jsx', '*.tsx', '*.vue', '*.svelte'], pattern: '<img(?![^>]*\balt=)[^>]*>'}

  - id: CORE-ACC-02
    title: No flashing content
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Nothing flashes more than three times per second.
    rationale: WCAG 2.3.1. Photosensitive seizure risk.
    improvement: Slow or remove flashing effects; offer a 'reduce motion' setting that respects prefers-reduced-motion.
    effort: low
    sources: [WCAG22, EAA, EN301549, W3C-233]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-ACC-03
    title: Inclusive design for children with special educational needs
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Adjustable speed and time limits, audio alternatives for text, captions, dyslexia-friendly
      typography options, and support for switch or keyboard-only play.
    rationale: Accessibility beyond the AA floor is what makes a learning product usable by every child.
    improvement: Add a settings panel for speed, audio, captions and font; test with SEN teachers.
    effort: medium
    sources: [WCAG22, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: security
  - id: CORE-SEC-01
    title: No secrets in the repository
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: API keys, tokens and passwords are not committed.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 32 (security of processing).
    improvement: Rotate the exposed key, move it to a secret manager, and add gitleaks to CI.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, pattern: '(sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}|-----BEGIN (RSA |EC )?PRIVATE KEY-----)'}

  - id: CORE-SEC-02
    title: Access control on every store of learner data
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Every table, bucket or collection with learner data enforces access control at the data
      layer (e.g. row-level security), not only in the client.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 25 and 32. Client-only checks are easily bypassed.
    improvement: Enable row-level security with policies scoped to class and role; add a test per table.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, globs: ['*.sql'], flags: i, pattern: 'disable row level security'}

  - id: CORE-SEC-03
    title: Encryption in transit
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: All network calls use TLS. No plain http endpoints for APIs or assets.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 32.
    improvement: Switch the URL to https and enable HSTS.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '[''"]http://(?!localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|0\.0\.0\.0|www\.w3\.org|schemas\.|xmlns)[^''"]+[''"]'}

  - id: CORE-SEC-04
    title: No personal data in logs
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Application logs contain pseudonymous IDs only, with short retention.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 32. Logs are often copied to third-party tools.
    improvement: Log the learner ID instead of names or emails; add a log scrubber.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(console\.(log|info|warn|error)|logger\.\w+|print)\s*\([^)]*\b(email|fullName|full_name|firstName|first_name|lastName|phone|password)\b'}

  - id: CORE-SEC-05
    title: Vulnerability handling and breach response
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      A published way to report vulnerabilities (SECURITY.md or security.txt), a process to fix them,
      and a breach procedure that lets controllers meet the 72-hour notification deadline.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 33. Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations for products with digital elements.
    improvement: Add SECURITY.md and an incident runbook with contact chain and timelines.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, CRA]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: security_policy_missing, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-SEC-06
    title: Strong authentication for adults, simple safe login for children
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Teacher and admin accounts use MFA. Children use age-appropriate login (class code,
      picture password, teacher reset) without email or phone collection.
    rationale: Adult accounts hold data on whole classes. Children should not need personal contact details to log in.
    improvement: Enforce MFA for staff roles; replace child email login with class codes.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- CORE: content
  - id: CORE-CNT-01
    title: Asset provenance and licences recorded
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Every image, sound, font and AI-generated asset has a recorded source, licence, author and,
      for AI assets, the model used.
    rationale: Copyright compliance and AI Act Art. 50 marking of generated content.
    improvement: Keep an assets/PROVENANCE.csv and check it in CI.
    effort: low
    sources: [AIA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-CNT-02
    title: Age rating self-assessment
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The product has a documented age-appropriateness assessment covering violence, fear, language,
      in-app purchases, contact risks and addictive features (PEGI-style descriptors).
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 16 and 17 foresee harmonised age ratings covering monetisation and contact risks.
    improvement: Run a PEGI-style self-assessment and publish the resulting age and descriptors.
    effort: low
    sources: [PEGI, KIDS]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ================================================================ PROFILE A: educational games
  - id: A-ECO-01
    title: No paid randomised rewards (loot boxes)
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A, B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No loot boxes, gacha, mystery chests or other variable rewards that can be obtained with
      money or with currency purchasable with money.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 13(2) bans variable reward systems on social and video services. DFA proposal bans paid loot boxes for minors in games.
    improvement: Replace with fixed, visible rewards earned through learning.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DFA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, flags: i, pattern: '(loot_?box|lootbox|gacha|mystery_?(box|chest)|openChest|randomReward|caixa_?mist[eé]rio|ba[uú]_?surpresa)'}

  - id: A-ECO-02
    title: No pay-to-win
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A, B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Nothing bought with money gives a gameplay or learning advantage.
    rationale: DFA proposal bans pay-to-win for minors. Fairness in learning.
    improvement: Make all progression earnable through play; keep any paid items cosmetic and adult-purchased.
    effort: medium
    sources: [DFA, UCPD]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(buy(Boost|PowerUp|Hint|Lives|Energy)|purchase(Boost|PowerUp|Hint|Lives|Energy)|comprar(Vidas|Energia|Dica))'}

  - id: A-ECO-03
    title: Virtual currency is not sold to children and shows its real value
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      In-game currency cannot be bought by a minor. If it can be bought by an adult, its value in
      euro is shown wherever it is spent, and it is off by default for children unless a guardian approves.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 13(1) (applied to chatbots via Art. 14(1)(c)). DFA proposal.
    improvement: Remove currency purchase from child screens; show euro equivalents; add guardian approval.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DFA, UCPD]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(buy(Gems|Coins|Diamonds|Crystals)|purchase(Gems|Coins|Diamonds|Crystals)|gemPack|coinPack|comprar(Gemas|Moedas|Diamantes))'}

  - id: A-ECO-04
    title: Rewards follow learning, not time or return visits
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [A, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Points, stars and unlocks are tied to learning progress or effort, not to time spent,
      number of sessions or returning at specific times.
    rationale: Aligning game mechanics with learning mechanics (LM-GM model) improves learning and avoids engagement-for-its-own-sake.
    improvement: Map each reward to a learning mechanic (Arnab et al. LM-GM) and remove rewards that only count time or logins.
    effort: medium
    sources: [ARNAB2014, KIDS-COM, R-DECI1999, R-SAILER2020, R-HIRSHPASEK2015]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: A-PLY-01
    title: No penalties for not playing
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      No energy systems that only refill by waiting or paying, no pets or worlds that decay or die
      when the child is away, no loss of benefits for missing days.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(d) applied to online games by Art. 15(1)(a).
    improvement: Remove decay and energy timers; let the world wait for the child unchanged.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DFA, R-RADESKY2022]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(energyRefill|staminaRefill|refillTimer|petHunger|decayRate|witherTime|cropsWither|energia_?recarga)'}

  - id: A-PLY-02
    title: Non-shaming failure and feedback
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [A, B]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Errors and failures are presented as part of learning, without ridicule, sad animations directed at the child, or public exposure.
    rationale: Psychological safety supports learning, especially for younger children.
    improvement: Review all failure states with an instructional designer; use encouraging, specific feedback.
    effort: low
    sources: [UNCRC-GC25, ARNAB2014]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: A-ASM-01
    title: In-game assessment is transparent and separated
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_assessment, assessment]
    requirement: >
      When gameplay is used to assess learning (stealth assessment), learners, teachers and guardians
      are told, assessment data is separated from general telemetry, and it is used only for the stated purpose.
    rationale: GDPR transparency and purpose limitation. AI Act Annex III(3)(b) if AI evaluates learning outcomes.
    improvement: Document what is assessed in the teacher guide and the child privacy notice; store assessment data separately.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, AIA, AIA-OMNIBUS]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: A-SOC-01
    title: Multiplayer limited to closed groups
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [A]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [multiplayer]
    requirement: >
      Multiplayer happens within teacher- or guardian-defined groups. Cross-group play only through
      adult-mediated pairing. The game cannot be used to lure children to other services.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 15(1)(c) and 15(2).
    improvement: Use class rooms with join codes controlled by the teacher; block sharing of external links and handles.
    effort: high
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ================================================================ PROFILE B: game-based applications
  - id: B-EVL-01
    title: High-risk path for systems that evaluate or place learners
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [B]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_assessment, ai_adaptive]
    requirement: >
      AI that evaluates learning outcomes, steers learning, assigns levels or monitors tests is
      treated as an Annex III high-risk candidate: risk management file, data governance, logging,
      human oversight, accuracy and robustness testing.
    rationale: AI Act Annex III(3). Obligations apply from 2 Dec 2027 under the Digital Omnibus.
    improvement: Open a risk management file now (templates/ai-risk-file.md) and record the classification decision.
    effort: high
    sources: [AIA, AIA-OMNIBUS]
    detection:
      method: manifest
      patterns:
        - {type: manifest, check: high_risk_without_risk_file, confidence: high}

  - id: B-EVL-02
    title: No camera-based or biometric proctoring of minors
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [B]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [assessment, ai_assessment]
    requirement: Tests are not proctored by webcam, eye tracking, keystroke biometrics or behaviour analysis of the child.
    rationale: AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) (emotion recognition) and Annex III(3)(d) (monitoring during tests). GDPR Art. 9.
    improvement: Use supervised test conditions in class instead of automated surveillance.
    effort: medium
    sources: [AIA, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(proctor|eyeTracking|gazeTracking|tabSwitchDetect|keystrokeDynamics|webcamMonitor)'}

  - id: B-EVL-03
    title: Results are explainable and contestable
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [B]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [assessment, ai_assessment]
    requirement: Teachers and learners can see why a result was given and can contest it with a human.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 22(3). AI Act transparency for high-risk systems.
    improvement: Show per-item evidence behind each score and a 'request review' action for teachers.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, AIA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: B-EVL-04
    title: Validity, fairness and accessibility of assessment
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [B]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [assessment, ai_assessment]
    requirement: >
      Assessment validity is documented, results are checked for bias across groups (gender,
      language background, SEN), and accommodations (extra time, audio) do not disadvantage learners.
    rationale: Good assessment practice and AI Act data governance expectations.
    improvement: Run a differential item functioning check on pilot data and document accommodations.
    effort: high
    sources: [AIA, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: B-UGC-01
    title: User-generated content is moderated and visible to the teacher
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [B, A, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ugc, chat]
    requirement: >
      Content created or uploaded by children is moderated proportionally to age, visible to the
      responsible teacher, reportable, and not public. Uploaded media has metadata (e.g. GPS) stripped.
    rationale: DSA Art. 28 guidelines. KIDS Act Art. 12(3) and 19.
    improvement: Add teacher review queues, EXIF stripping on upload, and keep galleries class-private.
    effort: medium
    sources: [DSA-G28, KIDS, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(isPublic|visibility)\s*[:=]\s*[''"]?public'}

  - id: B-UGC-02
    title: No photos of children's faces kept or shared beyond need
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [B, A, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ugc]
    requirement: >
      Photos and videos of children are only stored when necessary for the learning activity, are
      never public, expire automatically, and others cannot download them.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 12(3)(e). GDPR minimisation and storage limitation.
    improvement: Prefer avatars; add auto-expiry and disable download of child media.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: B-DAT-01
    title: Research use of learning data is separated
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [B, A, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Learning data is only shared for research under a data sharing agreement, with legal basis,
      ethics approval and pseudonymisation, and never as a by-product of normal operation.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 5(1)(b), 6 and 89.
    improvement: Create a research export pipeline that pseudonymises and logs every extract.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: B-SIM-01
    title: Sensitive simulations include warnings and debrief
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [B]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Simulations about health, conflict, loss or other sensitive themes include a content note, an exit at any time, and a guided debrief.
    rationale: Protects children from distressing content and supports reflection.
    improvement: Add content notes and a debrief screen designed with the instructional team.
    effort: low
    sources: [UNCRC-GC25, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: B-OPS-01
    title: Dashboards show learning, not surveillance
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Teacher and guardian dashboards show what helps learning; they avoid minute-by-minute activity logs and are explained to the child.
    rationale: Respect for the child's privacy and agency (KIDS Act Art. 20(1)(f), UN GC 25).
    improvement: Aggregate activity data and show learning progress instead of raw logs.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ================================================================ PROFILE C: gamified applications
  - id: C-ENG-01
    title: Streaks are optional and never punish
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [C, A]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [streaks]
    requirement: >
      Streaks can be switched off, carry no loss framing, and missing a day costs nothing (free
      freezes or no reset).
    rationale: "KIDS Act Art. 9(2)(d) (penalties for not engaging). DFA proposal: right to switch off streak rewards."
    improvement: Add a 'turn off streaks' setting and replace 'you will lose your streak' with neutral progress messages.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DFA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: high, flags: i, pattern: '(lose your streak|streak (will be )?lost|don''t break (your|the) (streak|chain)|perdes a tua sequ[eê]ncia|vais perder a sequ[eê]ncia|n[aã]o quebres a sequ[eê]ncia)'}
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(resetStreak|streakReset|breakStreak)'}

  - id: C-ENG-02
    title: Leaderboards are class-scoped and pseudonymous
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [C, A]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [leaderboards]
    requirement: >
      Leaderboards are limited to the class or group, show avatars or nicknames, can be disabled
      by the teacher, and never publicly rank named children.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 11(3) (social comparison). GDPR minimisation.
    improvement: Scope leaderboards to class, use nicknames, add a teacher toggle, and consider showing personal bests only.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, GDPR, DSA-G28, R-HANUS2015, R-SAILER2020]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(globalLeaderboard|publicLeaderboard|worldRanking|leaderboard[^\n]{0,80}(fullName|full_name|realName))'}

  - id: C-ENG-03
    title: Points and badges have no money value
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Points, badges and levels cannot be bought, sold or exchanged for money or goods.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 13. Keeps gamification about learning.
    improvement: Remove any purchase or exchange path for points.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DFA]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(buyPoints|purchasePoints|buyXp|purchaseXp|redeemForCash|pointsToCredit)'}

  - id: C-ENG-04
    title: No variable reward schedules designed for engagement
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [C, A]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Rewards are predictable and earned. Random bonus drops and slot-machine style surprises are avoided.
    rationale: Variable ratio rewards drive compulsive use. KIDS Act Art. 13(2) bans them in spending contexts on social and video services.
    improvement: Replace random bonuses with predictable milestones the child can see in advance.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, KIDS-COM, R-DECI1999, R-DIXON2013]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(randomBonus|surpriseReward|dailySpin|spinTheWheel|luckyDraw|roda_?da_?sorte)'}

  - id: C-ENG-05
    title: Engagement metrics balanced by wellbeing metrics
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [C, A]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: Product KPIs for minors include learning and wellbeing outcomes, not only time spent, sessions or retention.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 10(2) asks recommender optimisation to include quality and mental health metrics; good practice for every product.
    improvement: Add learning-gain and healthy-session-length metrics to the product dashboard and goals.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, KIDS-COM, EUKO, R-CERASOLI2014]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: C-ENG-06
    title: Challenges without anxiety timers for younger children
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [C, A]
    age_bands: [B1, B2, B3]
    requirement: Quests and challenges for under-13s avoid countdown timers and expiring rewards.
    rationale: Time pressure creates anxiety and drives compulsive return.
    improvement: Remove expiry from quests or extend them to the whole school term.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS-COM, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(expiresIn|countdown|timeLeft|questExpiry|tempo_?restante)'}

  # ================================================================ AGE-BAND MODIFIERS
  - id: AGE-B1-01
    title: Ages 3 to 5 use the product only with an adult in control
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [B1]
    requirement: >
      No child account with credentials, no text input, no external links, no notifications to
      the child, audio-first instructions, and any AI conversation only with an adult present.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 14(1)(d) and 15(1)(d): access below 13 only through tools for guardians.
      Art. 7(4)(b) sets 3 years as the floor for guardian-controlled access to video services.
    improvement: Route access through the guardian or teacher device; remove text inputs and outbound links.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, globs: ['*.html', '*.jsx', '*.tsx', '*.vue', '*.svelte'], pattern: '<a\s[^>]*href=[''"]https?://'}

  - id: AGE-B2-01
    title: Under 10, communication uses preset messages only
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [B1, B2]
    features: [chat, multiplayer]
    requirement: No free-text chat. Communication uses preset phrases or emojis. External links are behind an adult gate.
    rationale: DSA Art. 28 guidelines on contact risks; KIDS Act Art. 12 and 15(1)(c).
    improvement: Replace chat input with a preset phrase picker.
    effort: medium
    sources: [DSA-G28, KIDS]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(sendChatMessage|chatInput|ChatInput|freeTextChat)'}

  - id: AGE-B3-01
    title: Under 13, access is enabled and controlled by a guardian or the school
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [B1, B2, B3]
    requirement: >
      Below 13, access to online games and AI conversational features is enabled and controlled
      through tools for guardians (or the school in educational deployments).
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 14(1)(d) and 15(1)(d).
    improvement: Require a guardian or school account to activate the child's access and settings.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: AGE-B4-01
    title: Ages 13 to 15 respect the national consent age and limited features
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [B4]
    requirement: >
      Where consent is the legal basis, guardian consent is obtained below the national age of
      digital consent (13 to 16 depending on Member State). Social features follow limited-account rules.
    rationale: GDPR Art. 8. KIDS Act Art. 6(2) for social and video features (13 to 14 only with guardian-set limited accounts).
    improvement: Read the national pack for the consent age and add a guardian consent step below it.
    effort: medium
    sources: [GDPR, KIDS, EDPB-CONSENT]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: AGE-B5-01
    title: Ages 16 to 17 keep protective defaults
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [B5]
    requirement: >
      Older teenagers may change defaults themselves after clear information and explicit choice,
      but defaults stay protective and profiling-based recommendations stay off by default.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 11(2) (changes only above 15 with explicit consent) and 10(2)(b).
    improvement: Allow opt-in changes with a plain explanation; keep defaults protective.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ================================================================ CORE: design for learning (look, sound, motion)
  # From research gathered for the EDEH Quality Compass (Nov 2026). See framework/03-design-and-motivation.md.
  - id: CORE-ACC-04
    title: Moving content and sound can be paused
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Content that moves, scrolls or animates automatically for more than 5 seconds can be paused,
      stopped or hidden, and audio that plays automatically for more than 3 seconds can be paused
      or muted.
    rationale: WCAG 2.2.2 and 1.4.2 (Level A), within the AA target of the European Accessibility Act. Uncontrolled motion distracts all learners and harms some.
    improvement: Add pause and mute controls to every auto-playing animation, video and background audio.
    effort: low
    sources: [WCAG22, EAA, EN301549]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-ACC-05
    title: Colour is never the only cue
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Right and wrong answers, states and instructions are signalled by shape, text, icon or sound as
      well as colour.
    rationale: WCAG 1.4.1 (Level A). About 1 in 12 boys has a colour vision deficiency, so colour-only feedback fails several children in every class.
    improvement: Add icons or text (tick, cross, label) next to colour feedback; test screens in greyscale.
    effort: low
    sources: [WCAG22, EAA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-DES-01
    title: Motion and sound can be turned down or off
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The product honours the device's reduced-motion setting and offers in-app controls to reduce
      animation and sound, including motion triggered by the learner's own actions.
    rationale: >
      WCAG 2.3.3 (Level AAA) protects learners with vestibular disorders. Distracting motion and sound
      compete with the learning content for attention.
    improvement: Wrap animations in a reduced-motion check (CSS prefers-reduced-motion, useReducedMotion, platform accessibility APIs) and add 'calm mode' and sound sliders.
    effort: low
    sources: [W3C-233, WCAG22, R-SUNDARARAJAN2020]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: repo, check: reduced_motion_missing, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-DES-02
    title: Motion shows the content, not decoration
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Animation is used to show what is learned (a process, a change over time, a procedure).
      Decorative, celebratory or purely entertaining motion and interesting-but-irrelevant extras
      ("seductive details") are kept to a minimum.
    rationale: >
      Seductive details lower learning (g = -0.33, 58 studies). Animation that depicts the content
      improves it (g = 0.23, 140 comparisons). In e-books, story-carrying animation helps young
      children while hotspots and side games distract.
    improvement: For each animation, write down what it teaches. Remove or shorten the ones that teach nothing; move side games out of the learning path.
    effort: medium
    sources: [R-SUNDARARAJAN2020, R-BERNEY2016, R-TAKACS2015]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-DES-03
    title: Calm screens, especially under 8
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [B1, B2]
    requirement: >
      Few elements compete on screen at once (as a guide, no more than four interactive or animated
      elements on the main screen for under-8s), and help is available as audio or pictures, not text only.
    rationale: >
      Busy visual environments increase off-task time in young children and affect autistic children
      most. A content analysis of 200 apps for under-8s found 95% showed more than four elements on
      the opening screen.
    improvement: Audit each screen's element count; move secondary elements into menus; add spoken help.
    effort: medium
    sources: [R-FISHER2014, R-HANLEY2017, R-CAC2018, R-HIRSHPASEK2015]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-DES-04
    title: Fantasy does not blur facts for young children
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [B1, B2]
    requirement: >
      When teaching facts about the real world to young children, use realistic images and plain
      language. Talking animals, impossible events and fantasy framing are kept for stories and play,
      not for factual content.
    rationale: >
      Human-like animals with human-like language reduced fact learning in 3 to 5-year-olds.
      Fantastical events, more than pace, reduced executive function in 4-year-olds.
    improvement: Review factual units for young children; replace anthropomorphic narration with realistic visuals or clearly separate story from fact.
    effort: medium
    sources: [R-GANEA2014, R-LILLARD2011]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-DES-05
    title: Visual style matches the concept, especially in maths
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Abstract concepts use simple, schematic visuals. Graphs and diagrams carry no decorative
      pictures. Concrete images are used to start, then faded towards abstract representations.
      Pleasant colours and friendly faces are welcome where they do not compete with the content.
    rationale: >
      Pictures inside graphs led 6 to 8-year-olds to count the pictures; generic symbols transfer
      better than concrete ones. Schematic visuals outperform cartoon and realistic ones in learning
      games. Emotional design (pleasant colours, faces) improves retention (d = 0.39).
    improvement: Remove decoration from graphs and diagrams; plan concrete-to-abstract fading in maths sequences; keep warm, pleasant colour palettes.
    effort: medium
    sources: [R-KAMINSKI2013, R-WOUTERS2013, R-BROM2018]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-DES-06
    title: Celebrations are short and proportional
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Reward animations and sounds are brief, proportional to the achievement and skippable. Win
      sounds are not used to make small or no progress feel like a big win.
    rationale: >
      Each celebration is itself a seductive detail competing for attention. In slot machines, win
      sounds made players overestimate how often they won.
    improvement: Cap celebration length (e.g. under 2 seconds), scale them to the achievement, and allow skipping.
    effort: low
    sources: [R-SUNDARARAJAN2020, R-DIXON2013]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: dependency, confidence: medium, names: [canvas-confetti, react-confetti, react-canvas-confetti, js-confetti, party-js, confetti-js]}

  - id: CORE-DES-07
    title: No colour-psychology claims
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Design decisions and product claims do not rely on popular colour-psychology effects
      (e.g. "red lowers performance") that are not supported by robust evidence.
    rationale: The red-colour effect on cognitive performance does not survive correction for publication bias.
    improvement: Justify colour choices by function (contrast, coding, highlighting) and accessibility, not by colour-psychology claims.
    effort: low
    sources: [R-GNAMBS2020]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ================================================================ MOTIVATION (profiles A, B, C)
  - id: A-MOT-01
    title: No reward pile-up
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [A, B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The team keeps a reward inventory (points, coins, badges, streaks, levels, leaderboards,
      unlockables, celebrations) and records for each one whether it is given for learning or for
      showing up. No more than two layers are given for playing time, logging in or simply finishing.
    rationale: >
      Expected rewards for doing a task lower later intrinsic motivation (d = -0.36), more in children.
      Badges plus leaderboards lowered motivation and exam scores over a semester. Each extra layer makes
      rewards more expected and more controlling. Stacking is an inference from single-element studies.
    improvement: Write the reward inventory (one line per layer, 'for learning' or 'for showing up'); remove or convert layers given for showing up.
    effort: low
    sources: [R-DECI1999, R-HANUS2015, R-MEKLER2017, R-SAILER2020, R-RADESKY2022]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: repo, check: reward_layers, confidence: medium}

  - id: A-MOT-02
    title: Feedback informs, it does not control
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [A, B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Feedback says what the learner did well and why, and what to try next. Copy avoids controlling
      language ("you must", "you have to") and external goal framing ("do this to win coins").
    rationale: >
      Informational verbal feedback raised intrinsic motivation (+0.33). Controlling language and
      external goal framing undermined conceptual learning in 11 to 12-year-olds, while drill scores
      looked fine, so the loss is easy to miss.
    improvement: Rewrite feedback strings as specific, informational messages; review copy for 'must' and reward-centred goals.
    effort: low
    sources: [R-DECI1999, R-VANSTEENKISTE2005]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(you must (finish|complete|play|keep)|you have to (finish|play|keep)|play to earn|win (more )?coins|tens de (acabar|jogar|continuar)|joga para ganhar)'}

  - id: A-MOT-03
    title: The product works with rewards switched off
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [A, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The teacher can switch off points, leaderboards and celebrations, or turn competition into a
      shared class or team goal, and the activity still makes sense. Teacher materials include debrief
      prompts that turn rewards into information ("What did you do to earn that?").
    rationale: >
      Gamification's cognitive gains are robust, but motivational gains vanish in rigorous studies;
      competition combined with collaboration beats competition alone. Leaderboards reward those
      already ahead and hurt the weakest.
    improvement: Add teacher toggles for each reward layer and a 'team goal' mode; add debrief questions to the teacher guide.
    effort: medium
    sources: [R-SAILER2020, R-HANUS2015, R-HIRSHPASEK2015]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: A-MOT-04
    title: Room for curiosity
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [A, B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      The design includes open questions, things to explore, choices with consequences, and moments
      where learners explain their reasoning to each other. Success is not only a count of completed items.
    rationale: >
      Curiosity improves memory through the same reward circuit that responds to coins, and predicts
      achievement, more strongly for children in poverty. Intrinsic motivation predicts quality of work
      and well-being; incentives predict quantity. Intrinsic motivation already declines through school.
    improvement: Add at least one exploratory or explain-your-reasoning moment per unit; track learning quality, not only items completed.
    effort: medium
    sources: [R-GRUBER2014, R-SHAH2018, R-CERASOLI2014, R-HOWARD2021, R-LEPPER2005]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: A-MOT-05
    title: Helping and creativity are recognised, not paid
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [A, B, C]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Helping others and cooperating are not paid with points or items. Creative tasks reward creative
      quality with informative feedback, not mere completion.
    rationale: >
      Toddlers rewarded with a toy for helping later helped less. Rewards for completing creative tasks
      lower creativity; recognising creative quality with fair feedback can help.
    improvement: Replace point payouts for helping with acknowledgement; give creative tasks qualitative feedback instead of completion rewards.
    effort: low
    sources: [R-WARNEKEN2008, R-BYRON2012]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ================================================================ COMMERCIAL PRACTICES (KIDS Act Recital 31, Art. 13)
  - id: CORE-COM-05
    title: Purchases are labelled as purchases, in real time
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [purchases]
    requirement: >
      Before any purchase or spending of purchasable currency, the child is told in clear, age-appropriate
      words (and icons or audio for non-readers) that this is a purchase that costs real money, at the
      moment it happens, with the price in the national currency.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 13(1) and Recital 31: minors often do not understand the consequences of online
      transactions, so purchases must be labelled as economic transactions in real time. Binding for social
      and video services and AI chatbots (Art. 14(1)(c)); applied to games and learning apps as good practice.
    improvement: Add a purchase confirmation screen for child accounts that says "This costs money" with the euro price and requires an adult step.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, UCPD, DFA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-COM-06
    title: No design for impulsive or unwanted spending
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [purchases]
    requirement: >
      No one-tap or in-content purchases for children. There is a clear separation and friction between
      learning or play content and buying anything related to it (for example a separate adult area and a
      confirmation step). No spending prompts at moments of frustration, failure or excitement.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 13(2) and Recital 31: services must not be designed in a way that leads to excessive,
      impulsive or unwanted spending, including through separation or friction between content and
      purchases. DFA proposal targets the same practices.
    improvement: Move every purchase out of the child experience into a guardian or school area; remove purchase buttons from gameplay, results and failure screens.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DFA, UCPD, R-RADESKY2022]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(oneClick(Buy|Purchase)|oneTap(Buy|Purchase)|instantPurchase|quickBuy|skipPurchaseConfirm(ation)?|autoPurchase|purchaseWithoutConfirm)'}

  - id: CORE-COM-07
    title: No disguised advertising
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Paid promotion is never presented as learning content, game content or a character's own opinion.
      Any sponsorship, product placement or brand partnership is clearly identified as such, in words a
      child of the target age understands.
    rationale: >
      UCPD Annex I point 11 bans editorial content paid for by a trader without making that clear, and
      point 28 bans direct exhortations to children to buy. DSA Art. 26 requires ads on platforms to be
      clearly identifiable. KIDS Act Recital 31 names product placement, influencer marketing and
      sponsorship as tactics with particular persuasive effects on minors.
    improvement: Label any commercial content clearly (e.g. "Ad" or "Paid partnership" with an icon); remove promotion voiced by characters or tutors.
    effort: low
    sources: [UCPD, DSA, KIDS]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(sponsoredBy|isSponsored|productPlacement|brandedContent|paidPartnership|partnerContent|conte[uú]do patrocinado|patrocinado por)'}

  - id: CORE-COM-08
    title: No commercial content inside learning activities for children
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 3
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Learning activities for children contain no product placement, branded rewards, sponsored
      characters or influencer endorsements, even when labelled. Funding and partner credits, if any,
      appear only in adult-facing areas.
    rationale: >
      Children, especially under 8, struggle to recognise persuasive intent even when content is labelled.
      Recital 31 of the KIDS Act lists these tactics among those with particular persuasive effects on
      minors; UN General Comment 25 asks states to protect children from commercial exploitation.
    improvement: Remove brands and sponsored items from learning content; move partner credits to the teacher or guardian area.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, UNCRC-GC25, R-RADESKY2022]
    detection:
      method: manual

  # ================================================================ AI COMPANIONS AND CHATBOTS (KIDS Act Recitals 32-34, Art. 14)
  - id: CORE-AI-08
    title: Conversation memory is off by default
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      AI systems do not keep or reuse information from a child's previous conversations by default,
      except where necessary to protect the child's safety. Any memory is visible to the teacher or
      guardian and can be deleted.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 14(1)(b) and Recital 32: persistent conversational memory with minors must be disabled
      by default, to prevent accumulating sensitive data and reinforcing harmful interaction patterns.
      GDPR data minimisation and storage limitation.
    improvement: Start each session without past context; if continuity is needed for learning progress, store structured progress data (e.g. skills mastered), not chat transcripts.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(persistentMemory|longTermMemory|conversationMemory|memoryEnabled|rememberConversations|enableMemory)\s*[:=]\s*true'}

  - id: CORE-AI-09
    title: AI is re-tested regularly and monitored after release
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      AI features are evaluated for risks to children before release and at regular intervals afterwards
      (and on every model or prompt change). After release, incidents involving children are detected,
      logged, assessed and acted on, with a named owner.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 14(1)(e)(f) and Recitals 32 and 33. The legal duty of post-market monitoring does not
      apply to micro and small enterprises; CSEF applies it to every provider because the risk to a child
      does not depend on company size. Risk mitigations by the provider of the underlying general-purpose
      model (AI Act Art. 55) can be relied on in part, but are not sufficient on their own.
    improvement: Schedule the age-appropriate red-team set (CORE-AI-05) to run at least each term and on model or prompt changes; add an incident channel for teachers and guardians and a monthly review.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, AIA]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-AI-10
    title: An AI assistant inside a game or app is opt-in and easy to leave
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      When an AI chatbot or companion is a feature of a game, app or platform, it is not switched on
