      automatically, not displayed prominently (e.g. not pinned at the top of contacts or the home screen),
      children are not encouraged to use it, and they can turn it off easily at any time.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 14(2) and Recital 34, which cover AI companions and chatbots deployed as a functionality
      of online games and platforms, including where in-game purchases can occur.
    improvement: Default the assistant to off (or teacher-enabled), place it behind a neutral help entry, and add a visible "turn off assistant" setting.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, pattern: '(assistantEnabled|chatbotEnabled|aiChatEnabled|aiCompanionEnabled|autoOpenChat|autoStartAssistant|showAssistantOnStart)\s*[:=]\s*true'}

  - id: CORE-AI-11
    title: AI never nudges children to spend or towards ads
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [ai_generative]
    requirement: >
      AI tutors, characters and assistants never suggest purchases, upgrades, premium content or
      advertised products, and are not optimised for spending or engagement time.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Recital 31 names AI-enhanced nudging as a commercial tactic with particular effects on minors;
      Art. 14(1)(c) applies the economic transaction safeguards to AI companions and chatbots, and Recital 34
      extends safeguards to chatbots inside games with in-game purchases. AI Act Art. 5(1)(b) bans AI that
      exploits age-related vulnerability.
    improvement: Remove commercial goals from system prompts and fine-tuning data; add red-team prompts that try to elicit upsell and test that the AI refuses.
    effort: low
    sources: [KIDS, AIA, UCPD]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: regex, confidence: medium, flags: i, pattern: '(upsell|encourage (the )?(user|child|student|player) to (buy|purchase|upgrade|subscribe)|promote (the )?(premium|shop|store|subscription))'}

  # ================================================================ COMMUNICATIONS (KIDS Act Art. 12, 15(2), Recital 36; DSA)
  # Detection uses the communications inventory (tooling/comms.py). Absence of a safeguard in code is a
  # signal, not proof: many chat services configure moderation in a dashboard. Findings are REVIEW.
  - id: CORE-CHT-01
    title: Every communication channel is declared
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Every way children can communicate (text chat, direct messages, comments, voice, video, live streaming,
      multiplayer messaging) is declared in csef.yaml features and listed in the DPIA, with the service used
      and where data is processed.
    rationale: >
      Accountability (GDPR Art. 5(2)) and the DPIA require knowing every channel. Contact risks are the main
      reason the KIDS Act regulates online games (Recital 36). Undeclared channels escape every other check.
    improvement: Add the channel to `features` (chat, multiplayer, social or ugc) and to `third_parties`; update the DPIA.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR, KIDS, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: static
      patterns:
        - {type: repo, check: comms_undeclared, confidence: high}

  - id: CORE-CHT-02
    title: Report and block in every channel
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [chat, multiplayer, social, ugc]
    requirement: >
      In every channel, a child can report a message or user in one step and block any user without the
      blocked user being told who blocked them. Reports reach a person quickly, with the message kept as evidence.
    rationale: >
      DSA Art. 16 (notice and action) applies to hosting services. KIDS Act Art. 12(1)(d) (block without
      identity disclosed) and Art. 19 (child-friendly reporting). DSA Art. 28 guidelines.
    improvement: Add report and block actions to every message and profile; route reports to a moderation queue with priority for minors.
    effort: medium
    sources: [DSA, KIDS, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: repo, check: comms_report_block, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-CHT-03
    title: Moderation by people and by tools
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [chat, multiplayer, social, ugc]
    requirement: >
      Communication is moderated by named people (a teacher in school use, trained moderators otherwise) who can
      hide, remove, mute and suspend, supported by automated filters for text and images in the product's
      languages, with rate limits against spam. The level of moderation matches the age band.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Recital 36 lists cyberbullying, harassment, grooming, sexual exploitation, recruitment and
      radicalisation as contact risks in online games. DSA Art. 28 guidelines on moderation for minors.
    improvement: Give teachers or moderators hide/remove/mute/suspend powers; add a text filter (word list plus a moderation API) and image checks for uploads; add rate limits.
    effort: high
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28, DSA]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: repo, check: comms_moderation, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-CHT-04
    title: Direct messages only with approved contacts; groups only with agreement
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [chat, multiplayer, social, ugc]
    requirement: >
      Nobody can start a private conversation with a child unless the child (or, under 13, the guardian or
      teacher) has approved that contact. Children are added to groups only with their agreement. Nobody can
      pressure a child into approving contact.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 12(1)(a)(c) and 12(2), applied to online games by Art. 15(1)(c) for 12(1).
    improvement: Restrict direct messages to approved contacts within the class or group; require acceptance for group invitations.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: repo, check: comms_direct_messages, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-CHT-05
    title: No links, handles or contact details in children's messages
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [chat, multiplayer, social, ugc]
    requirement: >
      Messages to and from children block or warn on external links, social media handles, phone numbers,
      emails and addresses, so the product cannot be used to move children to other services.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Art. 15(2) and Recital 36 (restrict link-outs, warning messages, prevent enticing minors to other
      services); Art. 12(3)(c) (contact details of minors never shared).
    improvement: Filter URLs, handles and contact details before delivery; show a warning to the child and notify moderation.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: repo, check: comms_link_filter, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-CHT-06
    title: Voice, video and live streaming off by default
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: >
      Voice chat, video chat and live streaming are off by default, enabled only by a guardian or teacher for
      under-13s, limited to approved contacts, and children cannot host live streams by default.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 11(1) (camera, microphone) and Art. 12(3)(f) (no hosting of real-time transmissions by default). DSA Art. 28 guidelines.
    improvement: Default voice and video to off; add guardian or teacher activation; restrict to class groups; remove child-hosted streaming.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: repo, check: comms_voice_default_on, confidence: high}
        - {type: repo, check: comms_voice_video, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-CHT-07
    title: Children's shared media is protected
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [chat, multiplayer, social, ugc]
    requirement: >
      Images and files sent in messages are checked automatically, visible to the responsible teacher or
      moderator, and cannot be downloaded or forwarded by other users. Contact and account information of
      children is never visible to people they have not accepted.
    rationale: KIDS Act Art. 12(3)(a)(b)(e). DSA Art. 28 guidelines.
    improvement: Add image checks on upload, disable download and forwarding of children's media, and restrict profile visibility.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28, GDPR]
    detection:
      method: mixed
      patterns:
        - {type: repo, check: comms_media, confidence: medium}

  - id: CORE-CHT-08
    title: Safeguarding procedure for communication risks
    level: MUST
    tier: 2
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [chat, multiplayer, social, ugc]
    requirement: >
      There is a written safeguarding procedure with a named lead: how moderators recognise and escalate
      grooming, sexual exploitation, extortion, threats, self-harm signals and radicalisation; how evidence is
      preserved; when guardians, schools, hotlines and authorities are contacted; and how moderators are trained
      and supported.
    rationale: >
      KIDS Act Recital 36 names these contact risks. Code cannot show this; it is the human side of every
      other communication rule. DSA Art. 28 guidelines expect effective moderation and support for minors.
    improvement: Write the procedure with the DPO and a safeguarding lead; train moderators and teachers; test it with a tabletop exercise each year.
    effort: medium
    sources: [KIDS, DSA-G28, UNCRC-GC25]
    detection:
      method: manual

  - id: CORE-CHT-09
    title: Messages are kept only as long as needed
    level: SHOULD
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    features: [chat, multiplayer, social, ugc]
    requirement: >
      Messages have a defined retention period enforced by code, children and teachers can delete them, and
      reported messages are preserved only for the investigation.
    rationale: GDPR storage limitation (Art. 5(1)(e)) and erasure (Art. 17).
    improvement: Add a retention job for messages and keep reported messages in a separate, access-controlled store.
    effort: low
    sources: [GDPR]
    detection:
      method: manual

files.framework/questionnaire.yaml:
# CSEF boundaries questionnaire.
# Used by tooling/policy.py (terminal and local web form) to turn an organisation's answers into
# a company pack, a boundaries report and a plain-language staff policy.
#
# Boundary questions map to framework rules. The tier of those rules decides how an answer is read:
#   tier 1 = the law already requires it; tier 2 = proposals and official benchmarks; tier 3 = research.
# Answers can only make rules stricter. They never relax the law.
#
# Placeholders in plain-language text: {org} organisation name, {approvers} who approves exceptions.

version: 1

sections:
  - id: org
    title: Your organisation
    intro: Who you are and who owns these rules.
    questions:
      - id: org_name
        type: text
        label: Organisation name
        required: true
      - id: pack_id
        type: text
        label: Short id for your pack (2 to 8 lowercase letters, e.g. acme)
        help: Used in file names and rule ids, such as ACME-POL-01.
        pattern: '^[a-z]{2,8}$'
        required: true
      - id: jurisdictions
        type: multi
        label: Countries where your products are used
        help: EU law always applies. Country packs add national rules where one exists.
        options_from: packs
      - id: scope
        type: text
        label: Which products does this policy cover?
        default: All our products used by or designed for children
      - id: owner
        type: text
        label: Who owns this policy? (a role, e.g. CEO)
        default: CEO
      - id: approvers
        type: text
        label: Who can approve exceptions and sensitive features? (roles)
        default: Data Protection Officer or CEO
      - id: contact
        type: text
        label: Where should staff send questions? (a role, channel or shared mailbox)
        default: The Data Protection Officer

  - id: products
    title: Your products
    intro: What you build and for whom. This decides which questions come next.
    questions:
      - id: profiles
        type: multi
        label: What kind of products do you make?
        required: true
        options:
          - {value: A, label: "Educational games"}
          - {value: B, label: "Game-based applications and software (platforms, assessment, simulations)"}
          - {value: C, label: "Gamified applications (points, badges, streaks on top of learning)"}
      - id: age_bands
        type: multi
        label: Which ages use your products?
        required: true
        options:
          - {value: B1, label: "3 to 5"}
          - {value: B2, label: "6 to 9"}
          - {value: B3, label: "10 to 12"}
          - {value: B4, label: "13 to 15"}
          - {value: B5, label: "16 to 17"}
      - id: buyers
        type: single
        label: Who chooses or pays for your products?
        options:
          - {value: schools, label: "Schools or education authorities"}
          - {value: families, label: "Families"}
          - {value: both, label: "Both"}
          - value: other
            label: "None of these (free, publicly funded, sponsored or other)"
            desc: >
              Nothing changes in the rules: who pays does not decide whether children are protected. The EU KIDS Act
              proposal covers games "irrespective of whether the service is provided free of charge, against payment,
              or against hybrid remuneration" (Recital 12). The report adds a note on the education exemption.
        default: both
      - id: features
        type: multi
        label: Which of these mechanisms do your products have, or might have soon?
        help: >
          Pick everything that applies now or in the next year. Questions about mechanisms you do not pick are
          skipped. Each one shows what it means and where the official wording comes from.
        exclusive: none
        options:
          - value: accounts
            label: "Child accounts or logins"
            desc: >
              Children sign in or have a profile that keeps personal data. Under GDPR Art. 8, consent for children
              below the national digital consent age (13 in Portugal) is given or authorised by a parent.
          - value: multiplayer
            label: "Multiplayer or playing with others"
            desc: >
              Children share a game session with other users, at the same time or in turns. The EU KIDS Act proposal
              requires a high level of privacy, safety and security for "contacts between minors and other recipients
              of the game" (Art. 15(1)(c)).
          - value: chat
            label: "Chat or messages"
            desc: >
              Children send messages to other users: free text, voice, or preset messages, emoji and emotes. Preset
              emotes are still messages. Contact rules: EU KIDS Act proposal Art. 12 and Art. 15(1)(c) and (2).
          - value: ugc
            label: "Content children create and share (drawings, posts, uploads)"
            desc: >
              Anything a child makes that other users can see. Hosted content needs a way to report it (DSA Art. 16).
              The EU KIDS Act proposal treats "incentivising or rewarding minors to share content" with an
              indeterminate number of recipients as addictive design (Art. 9(2)(c)).
          - value: social
            label: "Social features (friends, profiles, likes, comments)"
            desc: >
              Friend lists, public profiles, likes, followers, comments. If being social is the main purpose, the service
              may count as an "online social networking service" (EU KIDS Act proposal Art. 3(2)), which has the
              strictest obligations.
          - value: notifications
            label: "Notifications"
            desc: >
              Messages to the child outside the activity: push, e-mail, badges. The EU KIDS Act proposal targets
              "notifications not triggered by, or not directly related to, the minor's interaction or activity on the
              service" (Art. 9(2)(b)).
          - value: streaks
            label: "Streaks (days in a row)"
            desc: >
              Counting or rewarding regular return. The EU KIDS Act proposal targets "incentivising engagement at
              regular times or with greater frequency, including through penalties or loss of benefits for failing to
              engage regularly" (Art. 9(2)(d)).
          - value: leaderboards
            label: "Leaderboards or rankings"
            desc: >
              Lists that compare children by score, speed or progress. Not named in the law; CSEF treats them as
              social comparison and asks for class-only, nickname rankings (rule C-ENG-02).
          - value: purchases
            label: "Purchases, subscriptions or in-app items"
            desc: >
              Anything paid with money, or with virtual currency bought with money. The minor must know "in real time,
              that this is an economic transaction" and virtual currency must show its value in euros (EU KIDS Act
              proposal Art. 13(1)).
          - value: assessment
            label: "Tests, grades or progress tracking"
            desc: >
              Scores, levels, grades or reports about what a child knows. This is about the data and how it is used,
              with or without AI.
          - value: ai_generative
            label: "Generative AI (chatbots, tutors, AI-made text, images or voice)"
            desc: >
              An AI system that produces text, images, audio or video. People must be told when they interact with AI,
              and AI-made content must be marked (AI Act Art. 50). Scripted dialogue written by people is not AI.
          - value: ai_assessment
            label: "AI that marks or evaluates learners"
            desc: >
              AI used "to evaluate learning outcomes" is high-risk under the AI Act (Annex III, point 3(b)), with
              obligations applying from December 2027.
          - value: ai_adaptive
            label: "AI that adapts levels, paths or access"
            desc: >
              AI that steers the learning process or decides "the appropriate level of education" a learner gets is
              high-risk under the AI Act (Annex III, point 3(b) and (c)). Fixed rules written by people are not AI.
          - value: recommender
            label: "Recommendations of content"
            desc: >
              A system that suggests or ranks content for the child: a "recommender system" in the sense of DSA
              Art. 3(s). Stricter rules for social and video platforms in the EU KIDS Act proposal (Art. 10).
          - value: none
            label: "None of these"
            desc: >
              All questions about these mechanisms are skipped and your guardrails file declares none of them. The
              scanner still reads your code: if it finds one (for example a chat or ads SDK), it reports it as
              undeclared, so nothing is missed by accident.

  - id: level
    title: Your level of ambition
    intro: The minimum level every product is checked against. Products can choose a higher level, never a lower one.
    questions:
      - id: minimum_level
        type: single
        label: Which minimum level do you choose?
        required: true
        default: "2"
        options:
          - {value: "1", label: "Level 1, Legal baseline: what the law requires today"}
          - {value: "2", label: "Level 2, Forward-compliant: also what is coming (EU KIDS Act proposal, official guidelines)"}
          - {value: "3", label: "Level 3, Best practice: also what research and experts recommend"}

  - id: boundaries
    title: Your boundaries
    intro: >
      For each practice, say how strict you are. "Never" makes it a red line: the scanner blocks it at every
      level, even on weak signals. "Only with approval" means a named person must approve it in writing.
      "Follow our level" means the framework rules for your level apply.
    groups:
      - id: money
        title: Money and advertising
        questions:
          - id: ads
            label: Advertising or ad tracking shown to children
            rules: [CORE-COM-01, CORE-COM-07]
            never: We never show advertising to children. We never track children for ads.
            level: We follow the law on advertising to children.
          - id: lootboxes
            label: Paid random rewards (loot boxes, paid card packs, gacha)
            rules: [A-ECO-01]
            profiles: [A, B, C]
            never: We never sell random rewards. Children always know what they get.
            level: Paid random rewards follow the framework rules for our level.
          - id: pay_to_win
            label: Paying to win, skip learning or get ahead of others
            rules: [A-ECO-02]
            profiles: [A, B, C]
            never: Nobody can pay to win or to skip learning.
            level: Paying to get ahead follows the framework rules for our level.
          - id: currency
            label: Virtual coins or gems that children can buy
            rules: [A-ECO-03, C-ENG-03]
            profiles: [A, C]
            never: Children never buy virtual coins. Points and badges have no money value.
            level: Virtual currency follows the framework rules for our level.
          - id: purchases
            label: Purchases that children can start themselves
            rules: [CORE-COM-04, CORE-COM-05, CORE-COM-06]
            features: [purchases]
            never: Only adults can buy. Children never see a buy button.
            approval: Any purchase flow needs written approval from {approvers}.
            level: Purchases follow the framework rules. Adults buy. Every purchase is clearly labelled.
          - id: commercial_learning
            label: Brands, sponsors or product placement inside learning activities
            rules: [CORE-COM-08]
            never: Learning activities never contain brands, sponsors or products.
            level: Commercial content follows the framework rules for our level.

      - id: attention
        title: Attention and pressure
        questions:
          - id: dark_patterns
            label: Pressure design (countdowns, fake scarcity, guilt messages, pre-ticked boxes)
            rules: [CORE-COM-03]
            never: We never use countdowns, fake scarcity, guilt messages or pre-ticked boxes.
            level: We follow the law on manipulative design.
          - id: streaks
            label: Streaks that children can lose
            rules: [C-ENG-01]
            features: [streaks]
            never: We never punish a child for missing a day.
            approval: Streaks need written approval from {approvers}. They are optional and never punish.
            level: Streaks follow the framework rules. They are optional and never punish.
          - id: notifications
            label: Notifications that bring children back
            rules: [CORE-SAF-02]
            features: [notifications]
            never: We never send notifications asking children to come back.
            approval: Notifications need written approval from {approvers}. They are off by default.
            level: Notifications follow the framework rules. Off by default, only about the child's own activity.
          - id: endless
            label: Autoplay, endless feeds or no natural place to stop
            rules: [CORE-SAF-03]
            never: Every activity has a clear end. No autoplay. No endless feeds.
            level: Stopping points follow the framework rules for our level.
          - id: penalties
            label: Penalties for not playing (decay, energy timers, losing progress)
            rules: [A-PLY-01]
            profiles: [A, C]
            never: Children never lose anything for taking a break.
            level: Breaks follow the framework rules for our level.
          - id: characters
            label: Characters without AI that act like a friend (mascots, guides, scripted companions)
            help: >
              Characters with dialogue written by people. Being friendly is fine, and remembering progress or past
              missions is normal save data. The concern is pressure: "I missed you", guilt when a child leaves, or a
              character that gets sad if the child does not play. That is manipulative design, which consumer law
              already forbids towards children, with or without AI.
            rules: [CORE-COM-03]
            never: Our characters never use friendship, guilt or "I missed you" to keep children playing.
            level: Our characters follow the law on manipulative design. No guilt, no pressure to come back.
          - id: leaderboards
            label: Public rankings of children
            rules: [C-ENG-02]
            features: [leaderboards]
            never: We never rank children publicly. Rankings, if any, stay in the class and use nicknames.
            approval: Leaderboards need written approval from {approvers}. Class only, with nicknames.
            level: Leaderboards follow the framework rules. Class only, with nicknames.
          - id: variable_rewards
            label: Surprise rewards designed to keep children playing
            rules: [C-ENG-04, A-MOT-01]
            profiles: [A, B, C]
            never: Rewards follow learning. We never use surprise rewards to keep children playing.
            level: Rewards follow the framework rules for our level.

      - id: contact
        title: Contact and communication
        questions:
          - id: strangers
            label: Contact from people outside the child's class or group
            rules: [CORE-SAF-05]
            never: Children never get contact from people outside their class or group.
            level: We follow the law on contact. No contact from strangers.
          - id: chat
            label: Free-text chat between children
            rules: [CORE-CHT-04, CORE-CHT-05, AGE-B2-01]
            features: [chat, multiplayer, social]
            never: Children never chat in free text. They use preset messages only.
            approval: Any chat needs written approval from {approvers}, with moderation, report and block.
            level: Chat follows the framework rules. Moderated, with report and block, no links or contact details.
          - id: voice_video
            label: Voice chat, video or live streaming
            rules: [CORE-CHT-06]
            features: [chat, multiplayer, social]
            never: We never offer voice chat, video calls or live streaming to children.
            approval: Voice, video or streaming needs written approval from {approvers}. Always off by default.
            level: Voice and video follow the framework rules. Off by default.
          - id: ugc
            label: Content that children share with others
            rules: [B-UGC-01, B-UGC-02]
            features: [ugc]
            never: Children never share content with others outside their teacher.
            approval: Sharing features need written approval from {approvers}. Teachers always see what is shared.
            level: Shared content follows the framework rules. Moderated, visible to the teacher, no faces kept.
          - id: multiplayer
            label: Playing with children from other classes or schools
            rules: [A-SOC-01]
            features: [multiplayer]
            profiles: [A]
            never: Multiplayer stays inside closed groups set up by a teacher or parent.
            approval: Open multiplayer needs written approval from {approvers}.
            level: Multiplayer follows the framework rules. Closed groups only.

      - id: ai
        title: Artificial intelligence
        intro: >
          These questions are only about AI systems. The AI Act (Art. 3(1)) defines an AI system as a machine-based
          system that "infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content,
          recommendations, or decisions". Fixed rules, scripted dialogue and choices written by people are not AI.
          Characters without AI are asked about in "Attention and pressure".
        questions:
          - id: emotion
            label: Emotion recognition (AI reading feelings from faces, voice or behaviour)
            help: >
              An "emotion recognition system" is "an AI system for the purpose of identifying or inferring emotions or
              intentions of natural persons on the basis of their biometric data" (AI Act Art. 3(39)). It is banned in
              education (Art. 5(1)(f)). A child choosing an emote, emoji or avatar mood is not emotion recognition: the
              child decides and nothing is inferred. If children send those emotes to each other, that is
              communication (see "Contact and communication").
            rules: [CORE-AI-01]
            never: We never use AI to read children's emotions.
            level: We follow the law. No emotion recognition on learners.
          - id: companions
            label: AI characters that act like a friend or remember conversations
            help: >
              The EU KIDS Act proposal defines an "AI companion" as "an AI system ... that provides sustained,
              personalised interaction or companionship which simulates or facilitates a social, emotional or
              interpersonal relationship with a user" (Art. 3(5)(c)). Its rules (Art. 14) apply to AI only. Characters
              with scripted dialogue are a separate question. Saving a child's progress or past missions is not
              conversation memory.
            features: [ai_generative]
            rules: [CORE-AI-06, CORE-AI-08]
            never: Our AI never pretends to be a friend. It does not remember conversations by default.
            approval: AI characters with memory need written approval from {approvers}.
            level: AI characters follow the framework rules. No simulated friendship, memory off by default.
          - id: genai
            label: Generative AI that children talk to or that makes content for them
            help: >
              AI Act Art. 50 applies to every AI that talks with people or makes content. The EU KIDS Act proposal's
              rules for a "general conversational chatbot" (Art. 3(5)(d), Art. 14) exclude AI limited to a specialised
              educational task, but CSEF applies the same safeguards to educational AI.
            rules: [CORE-AI-03, CORE-AI-05, CORE-AI-09, CORE-AI-10]
            features: [ai_generative]
            never: Children never talk directly to generative AI. AI content is made and checked by staff first.
            approval: Any generative AI for children needs written approval from {approvers}, with tests before release.
            level: Generative AI follows the framework rules. Always labelled, tested before release and re-tested.
          - id: ai_decisions
            label: AI deciding grades, levels or access without a person checking
            help: >
              High-risk under the AI Act when AI evaluates learning outcomes, steers learning or decides access or the
              level of education (Annex III, point 3). Scoring rules written by people are not AI.
            rules: [CORE-AI-07, B-EVL-01]
            features: [ai_assessment, ai_adaptive]
            never: A person always checks AI decisions about a child.
            approval: AI marking or placement needs written approval from {approvers} and human review.
            level: We follow the law. A person reviews AI decisions about learners.
          - id: ai_training
            label: Training AI models on children's data
            help: Using children's answers, texts, voices or behaviour to train or fine-tune any AI model, yours or a supplier's.
            rules: [CORE-AI-04]
            never: We never train AI on children's data.
            level: We follow the law. No training on learners' data by default.

      - id: data
        title: Data and privacy
        questions:
          - id: biometrics
            label: Face, voice or fingerprint identification, webcam proctoring
            rules: [CORE-DAT-08, B-EVL-02]
            never: We never identify children by face, voice or fingerprint. No webcam proctoring.
            level: We follow the law. No biometric identification of minors.
          - id: third_parties
            label: Sharing children's data with a company without a signed agreement
            rules: [CORE-DAT-02]
            never: Children's data never goes to a company without a signed agreement.
            level: We follow the law. Every provider has a signed agreement.
          - id: transfers
            label: Children's data stored or processed outside Europe
            rules: [CORE-DAT-03]
            never: Children's data stays in Europe unless a legal mechanism is in place and recorded.
            level: We follow the law on transfers outside Europe.
          - id: test_data
            label: Real children's data in development, testing or demos
            rules: [CORE-DAT-07]
            never: Real children's data never leaves production. We test with made-up data.
            level: We follow the law. No real learner data outside production.
          - id: analytics
            label: Session recording, heatmaps or third-party analytics on child screens
            rules: [CORE-COM-02, CORE-DAT-04]
            never: We never record children's sessions. Analytics never contain personal data.
            level: Analytics follow the framework rules. No personal data in events.
          - id: location
            label: Collecting children's location
            rules: [CORE-DAT-09]
            never: We never collect children's location.
            level: Location follows the framework rules. Off unless essential.
          - id: research
            label: Using learning data for research or product studies
            rules: [B-DAT-01]
            features: [assessment]
            never: Learning data is used only to run the product, never for research.
            approval: Research use of learning data needs written approval from {approvers} and a separate legal basis.
            level: We follow the law. Research data is separated.
          - id: access_control
            label: Learner data readable without access rules (e.g. open database tables)
            rules: [CORE-SEC-02]
            never: Every store of learner data has access rules. No exceptions.
            level: We follow the law. Access control on every store of learner data.

  - id: tools
    title: Tools, packages and words
    intro: Concrete things the scanner can find in code.
    questions:
      - id: forbid_sets
        type: multi
        label: Which kinds of packages should never appear in your products?
        help: Advertising SDKs are already blocked by the framework.
        options_from: dependency_sets
      - id: forbid_extra
        type: list
        label: Other package names you never use (one per line)
      - id: phrase_sets
        type: multi
        label: Block pressure and guilt phrases in these languages
        options_from: phrase_sets
      - id: phrase_extra
        type: list
        label: Other phrases that must never appear in child-facing text (one per line)
      - id: own_rules
        type: list
        label: Anything else you never do? (one per line, in plain words)
        help: Each line becomes a rule that a person checks in every review.

  - id: process
    title: How you work
    questions:
      - id: review_every_days
        type: single
        label: How often must each product review its manifest?
        default: "180"
        options:
          - {value: "90", label: "Every 3 months"}
          - {value: "180", label: "Every 6 months"}
          - {value: "365", label: "Every year"}
      - id: agent_instructions
        type: single
        label: Must every repository give AI coding agents these rules (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, Cursor rules)?
        default: "yes"

# CSEF source pack template.
#
# A pack extends the framework without forking it. Use it for:
#   - national laws and guidance (a country pack, e.g. packs/es.yaml)
#   - sector or procurement requirements (e.g. a Ministry's rules for digital resources)
#   - research and literature you want cited in reports
#   - your own company red lines (keep company packs in your product repo, e.g. .cses/packs/acme.yaml)
#
# How it is loaded:
#   - packs/<code>.yaml is loaded automatically when the manifest lists `jurisdictions: [<CODE>]`
#   - any other pack is loaded through `packs: [path/to/pack.yaml]` in the manifest,
#     or with `--pack path` on the command line
#
# Merge rules (enforced by the scanner):
#   - sources: added to the registry. An id may not clash with an existing one.
#   - rules: new rules. Use your pack id as prefix (e.g. ES-DAT-01). Same fields as framework/rules.yaml.
#   - amend: change an existing rule, only in the stricter direction:
#       add_sources   cite more sources on the rule
#       note          shown under the rule in reports (national nuance)
#       level         only SHOULD -> MUST
#       tier          only to a lower number (e.g. 2 -> 1 when your country already made it law)
#       add_patterns  extra detection patterns (e.g. local-language UI strings)
#   - parameters: free key/values shown in the report (e.g. digital consent age)
# A pack can never weaken or remove a rule. Waivers are the only way to accept a gap,
# and they need a named approver in the product manifest.

pack:
  id: xx                      # lowercase; also the prefix for new rule ids (XX-...)
  title: "Country or organisation pack"
  jurisdiction: XX            # ISO country code, or 'ORG' for an organisation pack
  version: "0.1.0"
  maintainer: "name or team"
  status: "Draft"

parameters:
  digital_consent_age: 16     # GDPR Art. 8 national choice (13 to 16)

sources:
  - id: XX-LAW-1
    title: "National law title"
    type: law                 # law | law-pending | proposal | guidance | standard | literature | news
    jurisdiction: XX
    status: "In force since ..."
    url: "https://..."
    verified: 2026-01-01

amend:
  - rule: AGE-B4-01
    add_sources: [XX-LAW-1]
    note: "Age of digital consent here is 16."

rules:
  - id: XX-EDU-01
    title: "Short title"
    level: MUST
    tier: 1
    profiles: [core]
    age_bands: [all]
    requirement: "What the product must do."
    rationale: "Why, in one or two sentences."
    improvement: "What a team should change to meet it."
    effort: low
    sources: [XX-LAW-1]
    detection:
      method: manual

    label: Quem escolhe ou paga os vossos produtos?
    options:

      families: {label: "Famílias"}
      both: {label: "Ambos"}
      other:
        label: "Nenhuma destas (gratuito, financiamento público, patrocínio ou outro)"
        desc: >
          As regras não mudam: quem paga não decide se as crianças são protegidas. A proposta EU KIDS Act abrange
          os jogos quer o serviço seja gratuito, pago ou com remuneração híbrida (considerando 12). O relatório
          junta uma nota sobre a exceção para a educação.

    help: >
      Escolha tudo o que se aplica agora ou no próximo ano. As perguntas sobre mecanismos que não escolher são
      saltadas. Cada um mostra o que significa e de onde vem a definição oficial.

      accounts:
        label: "Contas ou login de crianças"
        desc: >
          As crianças entram com conta ou têm um perfil com dados pessoais. Pelo RGPD (art. 8.º), abaixo da idade
          de consentimento digital (13 anos em Portugal) o consentimento é dado ou autorizado pelos pais.
      multiplayer:
        label: "Multijogador ou jogar com outros"
        desc: >
          As crianças partilham uma sessão de jogo com outros utilizadores, ao mesmo tempo ou à vez. A proposta
          EU KIDS Act exige um nível elevado de privacidade, segurança e proteção nos contactos entre menores e
          outros destinatários do jogo (art. 15.º, n.º 1, alínea c)).

          predefinidos continuam a ser mensagens. Regras de contacto: proposta EU KIDS Act, art. 12.º e art. 15.º,
          n.º 1, alínea c), e n.º 2.
      ugc:
        label: "Conteúdos que as crianças criam e partilham (desenhos, publicações, uploads)"
        desc: >
          Tudo o que uma criança faz e outros podem ver. Os conteúdos alojados precisam de forma de denúncia (DSA,
          art. 16.º). A proposta EU KIDS Act considera design aditivo incentivar ou recompensar menores por
          partilharem conteúdos com um número indeterminado de destinatários (art. 9.º, n.º 2, alínea c)).
      social:
        label: "Funcionalidades sociais (amigos, perfis, gostos, comentários)"
        desc: >
          Listas de amigos, perfis públicos, gostos, seguidores, comentários. Se o objetivo principal for social, o
          serviço pode ser um serviço de rede social em linha (proposta EU KIDS Act, art. 3.º, n.º 2), com as
          obrigações mais exigentes.
      notifications:
        label: "Notificações"
        desc: >
          Mensagens para a criança fora da atividade: push, e-mail, crachás. A proposta EU KIDS Act visa as
          notificações que não são desencadeadas pela interação ou atividade do menor no serviço, nem diretamente
          relacionadas com ela (art. 9.º, n.º 2, alínea b)).
      streaks:
        label: "Sequências (dias seguidos)"
        desc: >
          Contar ou recompensar o regresso regular. A proposta EU KIDS Act visa incentivar a utilização a horas
          certas ou com mais frequência, incluindo com penalizações ou perda de benefícios para quem não volta
          regularmente (art. 9.º, n.º 2, alínea d)).
      leaderboards:
        label: "Tabelas de classificação ou rankings"
        desc: >
          Listas que comparam crianças por pontuação, rapidez ou progresso. A lei não as nomeia; o CSEF trata-as como
          comparação social e pede rankings só da turma e com alcunhas (regra C-ENG-02).
      purchases:
        label: "Compras, subscrições ou itens na aplicação"
        desc: >
          Tudo o que se paga com dinheiro, ou com moeda virtual comprada com dinheiro. O menor tem de saber, em tempo
          real, que se trata de uma transação económica, e a moeda virtual tem de mostrar o valor em euros (proposta
          EU KIDS Act, art. 13.º, n.º 1).
      assessment:
        label: "Testes, notas ou acompanhamento do progresso"
        desc: >
          Pontuações, níveis, notas ou relatórios sobre o que a criança sabe. Trata-se dos dados e do seu uso, com ou
          sem IA.
      ai_generative:
        label: "IA generativa (chatbots, tutores, texto, imagem ou voz feitos por IA)"
        desc: >
          Um sistema de IA que produz texto, imagens, áudio ou vídeo. As pessoas têm de saber quando interagem com IA
          e os conteúdos feitos por IA têm de ser assinalados (Regulamento da IA, art. 50.º). Diálogos escritos por
          pessoas não são IA.
      ai_assessment:
        label: "IA que corrige ou avalia alunos"
        desc: >
          A IA usada para avaliar resultados de aprendizagem é de risco elevado no Regulamento da IA (anexo III,
          ponto 3, alínea b)), com obrigações a partir de dezembro de 2027.
      ai_adaptive:
        label: "IA que adapta níveis, percursos ou acesso"
        desc: >
          A IA que orienta o processo de aprendizagem ou decide o nível de ensino adequado de um aluno é de risco
          elevado no Regulamento da IA (anexo III, ponto 3, alíneas b) e c)). Regras fixas escritas por pessoas não
          são IA.
      recommender:
        label: "Recomendações de conteúdos"
        desc: >
          Um sistema que sugere ou ordena conteúdos para a criança: um sistema de recomendação no sentido do DSA
          (art. 3.º, alínea s)). Regras mais exigentes para plataformas sociais e de vídeo na proposta EU KIDS Act
          (art. 10.º).
      none:
        label: "Nenhum destes"
        desc: >
          Todas as perguntas sobre estes mecanismos são saltadas e o ficheiro de regras não declara nenhum. O
          verificador continua a ler o código: se encontrar um (por exemplo, um SDK de chat ou de anúncios), assinala-o
          como não declarado, para que nada escape por engano.

  # Boundaries
  ads:
    label: Publicidade ou rastreio publicitário mostrado a crianças
  lootboxes:
    label: Recompensas aleatórias pagas (loot boxes, pacotes de cartas pagos, gacha)
  pay_to_win:
    label: Pagar para ganhar, saltar a aprendizagem ou passar à frente dos outros
  currency:
    label: Moedas ou gemas virtuais que as crianças podem comprar
  purchases:
    label: Compras que as próprias crianças podem iniciar
  commercial_learning:
    label: Marcas, patrocínios ou colocação de produtos dentro das atividades de aprendizagem
  dark_patterns:
    label: Design de pressão (contagens decrescentes, falsa escassez, mensagens de culpa, caixas pré-assinaladas)
  streaks:
    label: Sequências que as crianças podem perder
  notifications:
    label: Notificações que fazem as crianças voltar
  endless:
    label: Reprodução automática, feeds infinitos ou falta de pontos naturais de paragem
  penalties:
    label: Penalizações por não jogar (perda de progresso, temporizadores de energia)
  characters:
    label: Personagens sem IA que agem como amigos (mascotes, guias, companheiros com guião)
    help: >
      Personagens com diálogos escritos por pessoas. Ser simpático não é problema, e lembrar o progresso ou missões
      anteriores é um dado de jogo normal. O problema é a pressão: "tive saudades tuas", culpa quando a criança sai,
      ou uma personagem que fica triste se a criança não jogar. Isso é design manipulador, que a lei de defesa do
      consumidor já proíbe em relação a crianças, com ou sem IA.
  leaderboards:
    label: Rankings públicos de crianças
  variable_rewards:
    label: Recompensas-surpresa pensadas para manter as crianças a jogar
  strangers:
    label: Contacto de pessoas de fora da turma ou do grupo da criança
  chat:
    label: Chat de texto livre entre crianças
  voice_video:
    label: Chat de voz, vídeo ou transmissões em direto
  ugc:
    label: Conteúdos que as crianças partilham com outros
  multiplayer:
    label: Jogar com crianças de outras turmas ou escolas
  emotion:
    label: Reconhecimento de emoções (IA que lê sentimentos no rosto, voz ou comportamento)
    help: >
      Um sistema de reconhecimento de emoções é um sistema de IA que identifica ou infere emoções ou intenções de
      pessoas a partir dos seus dados biométricos (Regulamento da IA, art. 3.º, ponto 39). É proibido na educação
      (art. 5.º, n.º 1, alínea f)). Uma criança escolher um emote, emoji ou estado de espírito do avatar não é
      reconhecimento de emoções: é a criança que decide e nada é inferido. Se as crianças enviarem esses emotes umas
      às outras, isso é comunicação (ver "Contacto e comunicação").
  companions:
    label: Personagens de IA que agem como amigos ou se lembram de conversas
    help: >
      A proposta EU KIDS Act define "companheiro de IA" como um sistema de IA que proporciona interação ou companhia
      continuada e personalizada, simulando ou facilitando uma relação social, emocional ou interpessoal com o
      utilizador (art. 3.º, n.º 5, alínea c)). As suas regras (art. 14.º) só se aplicam a IA. As personagens com
      guião são outra pergunta. Guardar o progresso ou as missões anteriores não é memória de conversas.
  genai:
    label: IA generativa com que as crianças falam ou que cria conteúdos para elas
    help: >
      O art. 50.º do Regulamento da IA aplica-se a qualquer IA que fale com pessoas ou crie conteúdos. As regras da
      proposta EU KIDS Act para "chatbots conversacionais gerais" (art. 3.º, n.º 5, alínea d), e art. 14.º) excluem a
      IA limitada a uma tarefa educativa específica, mas o CSEF aplica as mesmas salvaguardas à IA educativa.
  ai_decisions:
    label: IA a decidir notas, níveis ou acesso sem verificação por uma pessoa
    help: >
      É risco elevado no Regulamento da IA quando a IA avalia resultados de aprendizagem, orienta a aprendizagem ou
      decide o acesso ou o nível de ensino (anexo III, ponto 3). Regras de pontuação escritas por pessoas não são IA.
  ai_training:
    label: Treinar modelos de IA com dados de crianças
    help: Usar respostas, textos, voz ou comportamento das crianças para treinar ou ajustar qualquer modelo de IA, vosso ou de um fornecedor.
  biometrics:
    label: Identificação pelo rosto, voz ou impressão digital, vigilância por webcam em testes
  third_parties:
    label: Partilhar dados de crianças com uma empresa sem acordo assinado
  transfers:
    label: Dados de crianças guardados ou tratados fora da Europa
  test_data:
    label: Dados reais de crianças em desenvolvimento, testes ou demonstrações
  analytics:
    label: Gravação de sessões, mapas de calor ou analítica de terceiros em ecrãs de crianças
  location:
    label: Recolher a localização das crianças
  research:
    label: Usar dados de aprendizagem para investigação ou estudos de produto
  access_control:
    label: Dados de alunos legíveis sem regras de acesso (p. ex. tabelas de base de dados abertas)
